title: 1 Cor 6: once you were such—but you were washed, sanctified, justified
source_text: XV. Praeterea eodem in loco, Apostolus satis evidenter opponit praesentem fidelium statum, in quo a peccatis justificati erant, conditioni eorum praecedenti in qua flagitiis variis indulserant. Quae oppositio vana & nulla esset, si, etiam antequam illis renunciarent, & quum illis adhuc immersi jacerent, jam tum nihilominus erant justificati. Et haec quidem, inquit, eratis, nempe scortatores, idololatrae, moechi, masculorum concubitores, fures, avari, ebriosi, maledici, rapaces; sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, sed justificati estis, in nomine Domini Jesu, & per Spiritum Dei nostri.
pass_a_gloss: Further, in the same place the Apostle quite clearly opposes the present state of believers, in which they had been justified from sins, to their preceding condition in which they had indulged various shameful deeds. Which opposition would be empty and null if, even before they renounced those things and while they still lay immersed in them, they were nonetheless already then justified. And such were some of you, he says—namely fornicators, idolaters, adulterers, men who lie with males, thieves, the greedy, drunkards, revilers, swindlers; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.
pass_b_english: Paul contrasts their justified state with their former vices (1 Cor 6).
That contrast collapses if they were already justified while still immersed in sin.
